elements.title: Social Emotional Development Standard
elements.description: Social emotional development is the core of early care and education because it sets a firm foundation on which all other learning will take place.

elements.title: Self-Awareness
elements.description: The child demonstrates an awareness of self. Children develop a sense of personal identity as they begin to recognize the characteristics that make them unique as individuals and to build self-esteem.
elements.source_text:
Concept 1: Self-Awareness
The child demonstrates an awareness of self.

elements.title: Demonstrates self-confidence
elements.description: Acknowledges her own accomplishments and says, "I can hit the ball." Explains, "I'm learning how to take care of myself and my friends." Signs, "I can do it myself."
elements.source_text:
Demonstrates self-confidence.
a.
Acknowledges her own accomplishments and says, "I can hit the ball."
Explains, "I'm learning how to take care of myself and my friends."
Signs, "I can do it myself."

elements.title: Makes personal preferences known to others
elements.description: Chooses carrots over celery during mealtime. Tells friends, "I don't like that."
elements.source_text:
b. Makes personal preferences known to others.
Chooses carrots over celery during mealtime.
Tells friends, "I don't like that."

elements.title: Demonstrates knowledge of self-identity/autonomy
elements.description: Declares, "I'm the big brother," while looking at a family picture. Tells the teacher, "I'm at school while mommy is at work." Holds up three fingers and says, "I am this many."
elements.source_text:
Demonstrates knowledge of self-identity/autonomy.
C.
Declares, "I'm the big brother," while looking at a family picture.
Tells the teacher, "I'm at school while mommy is at work."
Holds up three fingers and says, "I am this many."

elements.title: Displays an awareness of similarities and differences between self and others
elements.description: Says, "My hair is curly and yours is straight." Points to shirt and then to friend's shirt, indicating that they are wearing the same color of shirt.
elements.source_text:
d. Displays an awareness of similarities and differences between self and others.
Says, "My hair is curly and yours is straight."
Points to shirt and then to friend's shirt, indicating that they are wearing the same color of shirt.

elements.title: Demonstrates developmentally appropriate cultural curiosity and responsiveness
elements.description: Wonders about a friend's seaweed snack and asks for a taste. The group widens the story time circle to make room for the child and their wheelchair. A guest speaker (parent) shares a storybook and song in their home language to the class.
elements.source_text:
e. Demonstrates developmentally appropriate cultural curiosity and responsiveness.
Wonders about a friend's seaweed snack and asks for a taste.
The group widens the story time circle to make room for the child and their wheelchair.
A guest speaker (parent) shares a storybook and song in their home language to the class.

elements.title: Recognizes and Expresses Feelings
elements.description: The child recognizes and expresses feelings of self and others. Children develop emotional literacy through the ability to identify and acknowledge their feelings and feelings of others through daily interactions.
elements.source_text:
Concept 2: Recognizes and Expresses Feelings
The child recognizes and expresses feelings of self and others.

elements.title: Associates emotions with words, facial expressions, and body language
elements.description: Describes the emotions of a character in a book. Signs, "I am mad" when asked how they feel.
elements.source_text:
a. Associates emotions with words, facial expressions, and body language.
Describes the emotions of a character in a book.
Signs, "I am mad" when asked how they feel.

elements.title: Identifies, describes, and expresses their own feelings
elements.description: Covers their eyes and says, "This is scary!" while listening to a story. Says, "I am happy today because it's my birthday!"
elements.source_text:
b. Identifies, describes, and expresses their own feelings.
Covers their eyes and says, "This is scary!" while listening to a story.
Says, "I am happy today because it's my birthday!"

elements.title: Identifies and describes feelings of others
elements.description: Approaches an adult and says, "That child is sad. They are crying." Says, "My mommy will be so excited to see my picture!"
elements.source_text:
C. Identifies and describes feelings of others.
Approaches an adult and says, "That child is sad. They are crying."
Says, "My mommy will be so excited to see my picture!"

elements.title: Expresses feelings of satisfaction in independent activities
elements.description: Independently peddles the tricycle with a smile on their face. Displays their clay structure and says, "Look what I did!"
elements.source_text:
d. Expresses feelings of satisfaction in independent activities
Independently peddles the tricycle with a smile on their face.
Displays their clay structure and says, "Look what I did!"

elements.title: Expresses empathy for others
elements.description: Sees a friend crying and then gives the friend a hug. Asks, "Are you ok?" after seeing a friend fall down.
elements.source_text:
e. Expresses empathy for others.
Sees a friend crying and then gives the friend a hug.
Asks, "Are you ok?" after seeing a friend fall down.

elements.title: Self-Regulation
elements.description: The child manages the expression of feelings, thoughts, impulses, and behaviors. Young children develop self-control as they acquire the ability to regulate their impulses with decreasing support from adults.
elements.source_text:
Concept 3: Self-Regulation
The child manages the expression of feelings, thoughts, impulses, and behaviors.

elements.title: Understands and follows expectations in the learning environment
elements.description: Uses walking feet when transitioning to the library. Puts the puzzle away, where it belongs, when finished.
elements.source_text:
a. Understands and follows expectations in the learning environment.
Uses walking feet when transitioning to the library.
Puts the puzzle away, where it belongs, when finished.

elements.title: Adjusts behavior and adapts to transitions, daily routines, and unexpected events
elements.description: Moves through activities independently. Stays with the group and follows the teacher during a fire drill.
elements.source_text:
b. Adjusts behavior and adapts to transitions, daily routines, and unexpected events.
Moves through activities independently.
Stays with the group and follows the teacher during a fire drill.

elements.title: Self-Regulation
elements.description: The child manages the expression of feelings, thoughts, impulses, and behaviors.
elements.source_text:
Concept 3: Self-Regulation
The child manages the expression of feelings, thoughts, impulses, and behaviors.

elements.title: Understands and follows expectations in the learning environment
elements.description: Uses walking feet when transitioning to the library. Puts the puzzle away, where it belongs, when finished.
elements.source_text: a. Understands and follows expectations in the learning environment.

elements.title: Adjusts behavior and adapts to transitions, daily routines, and unexpected events
elements.description: Moves through activities independently. Stays with the group and follows the teacher during a fire drill. Chooses a cozy corner away from the group when needed.
elements.source_text: b. Adjusts behavior and adapts to transitions, daily routines, and unexpected events.

elements.title: Chooses appropriate words and actions
elements.description: Says and/or signs, "Stop, I don't like it when you hit me." Waits their turn during a shared game or toy time.
elements.source_text: C. Chooses appropriate words and actions.

elements.title: Attachment
elements.description: The child demonstrates the ability to engage in and maintain secure relationships.
elements.source_text:
Concept 1: Attachment
The child demonstrates the ability to engage in and maintain secure relationships.

elements.title: Expresses interest, curiosity, and trust with familiar adults
elements.description: Child welcomes a new guest to the classroom. When teacher smiles, child responds with a smile back.
elements.source_text: a. Expresses interest, curiosity, and trust with familiar adults.

elements.title: Seeks support from familiar adults
elements.description: Asks for comfort/reassurance after a playground fall. Seeks out the caregiver when they need help doing a task.
elements.source_text: b. Seeks support from familiar adults.

elements.title: Separates from familiar adult with minimal distress
elements.description: Continues to paint after acknowledging a family member's departure. Transitions quickly into classroom activity after family drop off.
elements.source_text: C. Separates from familiar adult with minimal distress.

elements.title: Social Interactions
elements.description: The child displays positive social behavior.
elements.source_text:
Concept 2: Social Interactions
The child displays positive social behavior.

elements.title: Responds when adults or other children initiate interactions
elements.description: Selects from the choice board when asked, "What do you want to do now?" Decides whether to join a group when invited to play.
elements.source_text: a. Responds when adults or other children initiate interactions.

elements.title: Initiates and sustains positive interactions with adults and other children
elements.description: Shares about a new food at dinner. Suggests, "Let's build a road for our cars." Then the children work together to build a road.
elements.source_text: b. Initiates and sustains positive interactions with adults and other children.

elements.title: Acknowledges someone's perspective by demonstrating positive ways to resolve conflict
elements.description: Child asks, "When you're done, can I play with it?" Seeks assistance from a teacher when a disagreement starts to escalate.
elements.source_text: C. Acknowledges someone's perspective by demonstrating positive ways to resolve conflict.

elements.title: Respect
elements.description: The child has an increasing capacity to understand social boundaries about behavior and the environment.
elements.source_text:
Concept 3: Respect
The child has an increasing capacity to understand social boundaries about behavior and the environment.

elements.title: Respects the rights and property of others
elements.description: Walks around a block structure built by another child. Waits behind friend for their turn to go down the slide.
elements.source_text: a. Respects the rights and property of others.

elements.title: Defends own rights and the rights of others
elements.description: Tells his friend not to knock down his block structure. Tells teacher, "I can't have anything with peanuts."
elements.source_text: b. Defends own rights and the rights of others.

elements.title: Shows respect for learning materials in the learning environment
elements.description: Stacks up books after reading time. Puts caps on markers after using them.
elements.source_text: C. Shows respect for learning materials in the learning environment.
